liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **BERTHA** (1 review): Garcia sings 'laughing and drinking that wine' instead of 'bragging' in this first Bertha [17]
- **WHARF RAT** (1 review): The transition from Wharf Rat into Dark Star is cited as a favorite jam [14]
- **BEAUTIFUL JAM�** (1 review): Included on the So Many Roads box set, this three-minute jam is highlighted [13]
- **DARK STAR//** (1 review): Jerry builds searing emotional intensity during the first Dark Star performance of the night [16]

## The recordings

- **gd1971-02-18.aud.cooper.123539.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 39 songs; 200 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd71-02-18.sbd.stephens.6672.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 157 min; rated 4.68/5 by 25 [3]. Said about its sound: This version has a high pitch problem caused by using 48,000 instead of 44,100 sampling; Nasty mic feedback during Bertha and an annoying whine around 8000Hz remain intact [3][24]
- **gd1971-02-18.sbd.cantor-crouch-diebert-gmb.85478.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 25 songs; 154 min; rated 4.57/5 by 23 [4]
- **gd71-02-18.sbd.orf.107.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 152 min; rated 4.33/5 by 69 [5]. Said about its sound: The mix receives 4.5 stars, while the sound quality gets 4 stars [17]

## Around the show

- Stage talk about: BAND by MARMADUKE, MARMADUKE by JERRY [1]
- The reviewer was born on the day of this concert, making it their first day [16]
- Mickey Hart's last performance until 1975-76 tours marks the rebirth of the band's sound [19]
- First New York appearance of Bertha and Pump Man, with Jerry fired up on pedal steel [1]
- The listener prefers the February 19, 1971 show for playing and song selection [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-02-18.aud.cooper.123539.flac16**: taped by Jim Cooper; source: AUD. Recorded on cassette tape by Jim Cooper > Hitachi Trq-222, 2 unidentified mikes. Transferred > Sony tc we475 > dbx 2231 EQ > sony rcd w500c > CDR > WAV >… [1]
- **gd71-02-18.sbd.stephens.6672.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Dan Stephens and Scott Thompson; source: Soundboard (no remastering) [3]. Also: Direct copy of the WBOTB tape circulated in 1996, with no digital processing except resampling [3]
- **gd1971-02-18.sbd.cantor-crouch-diebert-gmb.85478.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Betty Cantor; transferred by Chris L.; source: 7" two track BBD reel w/ Dolby A @ 7 1/2 ips > PCM501ES (beta) > PCM501ES analog out > Dolby A decoder > Apogee filter > analog in PCMF1/PCM501ES analog out >… [4]. Also: Reel flip at 04:48 of Saint Stephen was crossfaded during the transfer process [4]
- **gd71-02-18.sbd.orf.107.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Leigh Orf; source: Soundboard (remastered) [5]. Also: The recording fits on two 80-minute discs, with specific track durations listed for each set [20]

## Art and photos

- Poster by The Capitol Theatre: [Posters](https://merch.thecapitoltheatre.com/collections/posters?page=2) [26]
- Poster by crepuscularthad.blogspot.com: [Brokedown Palace: The Capitol Theatre and the Grateful Dead](https://crepuscularthad.blogspot.com/2017/03/capitol-theatre-and-grateful-dead.html) [27]
